lines: Morgan Kim
+1 (555) 010-8173 | morgan.kim@example.com | example.com/code/mkim
EDUCATION
Clearwater Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2017 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Clearwater Sensors | Hardware Test Engineer | Metro City, USA | Apr 2022 - Feb 2023
- Automated end-of-line tests for a humidity sensor, cutting test time per unit from 90 to 25 seconds across 20,000 units a month.
- Traced a batch of early field failures to a solder-paste change; the findings updated the reflow profile and cut returns from 2.1% to 0.4%.
- Wrote the calibration procedure for the sensor line, cutting calibration drift complaints from 15 to 2 a quarter.
- Designed a test fixture that checked 8 boards at once, raising station throughput from 40 to 150 boards an hour.
Voltline Robotics | Embedded Software Engineer | Metro City, USA | Mar 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved update speed by 60% by compressing firmware images and resuming interrupted downloads.
- Wrote a hardware-in-the-loop test rig that ran 400 motor-control tests on every firmware build.
- Added a crash logger that saved the last 2 seconds of sensor data to flash, which found the root cause of 5 field failures.
- Sampled the motor's 5 kHz vibration signal at 8 kHz so the fault detector could capture it without aliasing.
- Fixed a race condition on the counter shared by the interrupt handler and the main loop by declaring the counter volatile.
- Rewrote the motor-controller firmware for a warehouse robot fleet of 300 units, cutting control-loop jitter from 120 to 15 microseconds and field motor faults by 60%.
PROJECTS
Low-Power Weather Station | Independent Project | C, STM32 | Jan 2025 - Present
- Engineered a next-generation, innovation-driven IoT solution that redefines sustainable environmental sensing.
- Cut average current from 4.2 mA to 0.9 mA by sleeping between readings and batching radio transmissions.
- Published the schematics and firmware openly, and a local school built two stations from them.
Formula Student Electric Car | Electronics Lead, Team of 12 | C | Sep 2019 - May 2021
- Worked on firmware and testing for the robot fleet's motor controllers.
- The CAN-bus firmware for the dashboard was written and tested against the motor controller before each race.
- Rewrote motor-control firmware for a fleet of about 300 robots, cutting control-loop jitter eightfold and motor faults by more than half.
SKILLS
Tools: C, C++, STM32, oscilloscopes
Methods: firmware, hardware-in-the-loop testing, CAN, low-power design

items.says: Make the code link open directly to relevant, working code or project documentation.
items.because: A general profile is less useful if a reviewer has to hunt for your work.

items.says: Put the more recent Voltline role above Clearwater Sensors.
items.because: Experience should run newest to oldest so your current level of work is visible first.

items.says: Clarify what part of the end-of-line test process you automated.
items.because: It helps establish your technical contribution.

items.says: Clarify whether the drop in complaints can reasonably be attributed to the calibration procedure.
items.because: That makes the causal claim more credible.

items.says: Specify whether the 60% improvement means download time, total update time, or transfer rate.
items.because: Compression and interrupted-download recovery solve different problems, so the metric is ambiguous.

items.says: Add the relevant hardware or test scope if it demonstrates a skill required by target jobs.
Say the recorded data enabled diagnosis rather than suggesting the logger found root causes.
Sampling a 5 kHz signal at 8 kHz does not capture it without aliasing.
items.because: That would require a sampling rate above 10 kHz, or a different explanation of the measured signal.

items.says: Declaring a shared counter volatile does not by itself fix a race condition.
items.because: It does not make access atomic.

items.says: Be ready to explain how the field-fault reduction was measured.
Remove the promotional language.
items.because: It does not tell a reviewer what you built or how.

items.says: If relevant, specify the operating conditions used for the current measurements.
items.because: That would show the measurements are comparable.

items.says: State the responsibilities you actually held as electronics lead.
items.because: The current bullets do not show how you led the team of 12.

items.says: The bullet discusses a robot fleet rather than the electric car.
items.because: As written, it undermines confidence in the rest of the resume.

items.says: Make your own role in writing and testing the CAN-bus firmware explicit.
items.because: The passive construction obscures your contribution.

items.says: The bullet discusses a robot fleet rather than the electric car.
items.because: As written, it undermines confidence in the rest of the resume.

items.says: The bullet substantially duplicates the Voltline motor-controller achievement.
items.because: As written, it undermines confidence in the rest of the resume.

items.says: Separate languages, hardware or platforms, and lab tools more consistently.
items.because: A more specific skills list is more useful.

items.says: Separate methods more consistently from the other skill categories.
items.because: A more specific skills list is more useful.

items.says: Use specific, substantiated tools or protocols instead of broad terms such as “firmware.”
items.because: That makes the skills list more useful.
